patients.summary: Retail store manager with PCOS on metformin, iron deficiency anemia and generalized anxiety who joined in early pregnancy in 2022. That pregnancy carried a fetal gastroschisis; a second in 2025 carried a fetal myelomeningocele, late virilizing ovarian enlargement and acute fatty liver of pregnancy found at a 37-week cesarean admission, with full recovery by her last visit.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish primary care here, moving her care over from a practice she has not seen in over a year. Currently pregnant, about 10 weeks, and already has an OB group lined up for the pregnancy. Takes metformin and an iron pill. Booked new patient visit 6/8 at 8:40. documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28 y/o woman here to set up primary care. She is pregnant, roughly 10.5 weeks by an LMP of 3/25/22, and already has a first appointment with an outside OB group, which will manage the pregnancy. One prior pregnancy, no problems, healthy term baby.

PCOS: diagnosed years ago for irregular cycles. On metformin 500 twice a day, tolerating it. OB knows she is on it.
Iron deficiency anemia: has been on ferrous sulfate daily for a few years, tolerating it. No bleeding history beyond periods.
Anxiety (GAD): long-standing worry, sleep fine most nights. Never been on medication for it, not in counseling now. Feels it is manageable.
Also taking a prescription prenatal with 4 mg folate.

PSH: tonsils out at 12. Laparoscopic R ovarian cystectomy at 24 for a bleeding corpus luteum cyst.
Allergies: latex (hives, type I) and sulfa (rash).
Family: mother with T2DM, father with hypertension, a paternal aunt with lupus, and a cousin on her mother's side born with myelomeningocele.
Social: manages a retail store, long days on her feet. Married. Has never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. Vitals as recorded. Thyroid normal size. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin without rash.

GAD-7 6, PHQ-9 3.

A/P
1. PCOS - continue metformin 500 BID for now, defer to OB on whether to continue through pregnancy. A1c with labs.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - continue ferrous sulfate. CBC, iron studies today.
3. GAD - mild by score. Talked through what helps her; recheck at future visits.
4. Early pregnancy - prenatal care with OB. Continue the high-dose folate prenatal.
5. Health maintenance - hep C and HIV screening with today's blood work. Records release signed for her old office.
RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Shannon, your labs are back. Hemoglobin is a little low at 11.6 and your iron stores (ferritin 19) are on the low side, so please keep taking the iron every day. Kidney, liver and thyroid tests are normal, A1c is normal at 5.4, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Nothing else to do for now. Let me know if the iron is bothering your stomach.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Prior practice records received, 31 pages, indexed under outside records.
Summary for PCP: problem list PCOS, iron deficiency anemia, generalized anxiety. Meds metformin 500 BID, ferrous sulfate daily. Allergies latex, sulfa. Last cervical cytology 2020: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. Last office visit early 2021. Immunizations: childhood series documented, Tdap in her prior pregnancy, influenza 2020.

conditions.label: Gastroschisis
conditions.note: fetal anterior abdominal wall defect on anatomy ultrasound

reports.text: Transabdominal obstetric ultrasound. Single live intrauterine pregnancy, biometry consistent with 16 weeks. Fetal heart activity present. Amniotic fluid volume normal. Placenta posterior, no previa. Intracranial anatomy and spine visualized without evidence of a neural tube defect. Anterior abdominal wall defect to the right of a normally inserted umbilical cord with free-floating loops of bowel outside the abdomen, no covering membrane. Stomach and bladder seen. Limbs present.
reports.conclusion: Single fetus with gastroschisis. Normal amniotic fluid. No neural tube defect.

documents.title: Obstetrics prenatal visit letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group, letter to primary care.
Date of visit: 7/15/2022
Re: Shannon Wagner, G2P1001, 16w0d by LMP

Thank you for allowing us to share her care. She feels well today without complaint. BP 120/78, HR 72. Fundal size appropriate for 16 weeks.

Her second trimester quad screen returned with a markedly raised AFP at 3.9 MoM; hCG, unconjugated estriol and inhibin A were within normal limits. We performed a detailed ultrasound today: single fetus, normal fluid, no sign of an open neural tube defect, but there is a full-thickness abdominal wall defect with herniated bowel, consistent with gastroschisis.

We reviewed the finding with her at length. Plan: serial growth scans, antenatal testing in the third trimester, consultation with pediatric surgery, and delivery planned at a center with neonatal surgical capability. Continue prenatal vitamin with folate, iron and metformin.

Allergies: latex, sulfa.
Obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine consult to follow.

documents.title: PCP call after OB letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called her after reading the OB letter about the abdominal wall defect on the scan. She has had a few rough nights but says the OB team explained things well and the surgery plan for the baby made her feel better. Husband is with her on all the appointments. Sleeping ok most nights. Offered a visit sooner if the worry gets ahead of her; she will reach out. Next visit with me in Sept as planned.

documents.title: Obstetrics prenatal visit letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group, letter to primary care.
Date of visit: 8/5/2022
Re: Shannon Wagner, 19w0d, known fetal gastroschisis

Routine visit. She feels well and has no concerns. Aside from the fetal finding, the maternal course has been smooth. BP 120/75, pulse 78. Exam unremarkable, no swelling of the legs.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, Hct 33%. BUN 8, creatinine 0.5. 24-hour urine protein 150 mg, within the normal range for pregnancy and useful as a baseline.

Plan: continue iron and prenatal vitamin. Growth ultrasound in 4 weeks. Pediatric surgery prenatal consult is being arranged.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.

documents.title: Obstetrics problem visit letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group, letter to primary care.
Date of visit: 8/24/2022
Re: Shannon Wagner, 29 y/o, 21w5d, pregnancy with fetal gastroschisis

She came in with five days of sharp, on-and-off pain low on the right side of the abdomen and pelvis. It catches her when she moves quickly or rolls over in bed and at times shoots into the right groin and labia. No bleeding, no tightening or contractions, no burning or frequency with urination.

She also mentioned itching all over for about the last week and a half, worse at night, without any rash.

Exam: abdomen soft, mild discomfort only with deep pressure in the right lower quadrant. Fundus at the umbilicus, appropriate for dates. Cervix long and closed. Skin with no rash and no excoriations.

Liver panel normal. Total bile acids 3.8 umol/L (normal).

Assessment:
1. Round ligament pain from the growing uterus. Reassured; position changes slowly, warm compresses, a support belt if helpful.
2. Itching of pregnancy without rash, normal liver tests and bile acids: physiologic pruritus gravidarum. Emollients, cool showers. Call if it worsens or concentrates on the palms and soles.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for the 3 month check. Now about 25-26 weeks. OB following closely for the baby's gastroschisis, growth scans so far ok per her. Had the round ligament pain episode in August, now gone. Itching has calmed down with lotion. Anxiety a bit higher since the diagnosis, mostly at night, still working full time. Taking iron, prenatal and metformin daily.

O: Vitals reviewed, weight up as expected for dates. Looks well. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.
GAD-7 8.
OB labs from August reviewed: Hgb 11.2.

A/P:
1. GAD - modestly higher in the setting of a stressful pregnancy. Talked about sleep, limiting late-night searching online, leaning on her husband. She prefers to keep going as is.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - stable for pregnancy. Continue iron.
3. PCOS - metformin continuing per OB.
Flu shot next month. RTC after delivery.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery service.
Admitted: 12/9/2022  Discharged: 12/11/2022
Patient: Shannon Wagner, 29 y/o G2P1001 at 37w0d

Indication: scheduled induction at 37 weeks for known fetal gastroschisis, delivery at a center with neonatal surgery.

Course: induction of labor. Uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery the same evening. Estimated blood loss within normal range. Infant taken to the NICU by the neonatal and pediatric surgery teams for abdominal wall repair. Mother recovered without complication; afebrile, ambulating, voiding, pain well controlled.

Allergies: latex (latex-free precautions throughout), sulfa.
Discharge meds: continue prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate, metformin 500 mg twice daily.
Follow-up: postpartum visit with obstetrics in 6 weeks; primary care as scheduled.
Now G2P2002.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subjective: About 6 weeks out from a vaginal delivery on 12/9 (induced at 37 wks for the baby's gastroschisis, summary in chart). Saw OB for the postpartum check last week, told she is healing fine. Baby had the repair in the NICU. She is tired, sleep broken, but says mood is ok and she is coping. Some worry but less than in the fall. Back on her usual routine with iron, prenatal and metformin. Planning to go back to work next month.

Objective: Vitals reviewed. Looks tired but bright. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft. No calf tenderness.
PHQ-9 5, GAD-7 7.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Postpartum, mood screen reassuring. Reviewed warning signs of postpartum depression; she knows to message.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC and iron studies today, continue ferrous sulfate.
3. PCOS - continue metformin.
4. GAD - stable.
Physical in June.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your hemoglobin is 11.4 and ferritin 15, both a little lower than in June, which is common after a delivery. Keep up the iron every day. We will check again at your physical.

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks! Will do. Is it ok to take it with my coffee in the morning or should I switch?

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Better away from coffee or tea, which block absorption. With a little orange juice or on an empty stomach works best if your stomach tolerates it.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29F for her yearly physical. Six months postpartum and back at the store full time. Feels like herself again. Periods have not returned in a regular pattern yet, which is typical for her with PCOS. Anxiety calmer, sleeping better now the baby sleeps longer stretches. Takes metformin, iron, prenatal.

ROS otherwise negative.
Meds/allergies reviewed. Latex, sulfa.

Exam: Vitals reviewed. NAD. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, well-healed laparoscopy scars. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix without lesion, Pap collected. Extremities without edema. Skin without notable lesions. Mood bright.
PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 5.

A/P:
1. Health maintenance - Pap today (last 2020, normal). Fasting labs drawn. Hep C/HIV already done 2022. Flu shot in the fall.
2. PCOS - metformin, A1c today.
3. Iron deficiency anemia - recheck CBC and iron.
4. GAD - mild, stable.
Return in about 6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, age 30. Store was short-staffed this spring and she has been covering extra shifts; more worry and trouble switching off at night. No panic episodes. Not interested in changing anything right now, wants to see if it eases as staffing improves. Kids keep her busy.
Meds: metformin 500 bid, ferrous sulfate, prenatal. Allergies latex, sulfa.

PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 9.

2. PCOS - stable on metformin. A1c, lipids today.
3. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC, iron studies.
4. HM - Pap current (2023). Flu vaccine this fall.

documents.title: Your results

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from her car at work, consented to telehealth, two identifiers confirmed.
Follow-up on anxiety from the summer. Staffing sorted out in the fall and she feels steadier, sleeping better. GAD-7 7, PHQ-9 3. Cycles remain irregular, longest gap about 3 months. Taking metformin and iron. No new concerns.
Assessment: GAD mild and improved. PCOS stable. Iron deficiency anemia on replacement, labs at the June physical.
Plan: no changes. Physical in June.

documents.title: Pregnant?!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Well, surprise. Took a home test after feeling off for a couple of weeks and it's positive, and a second one too. My periods are all over the place so I honestly didn't think about it. I have no idea how far along I am. What should I do first? Keep taking the metformin?

documents.title: RE: Pregnant?!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, and thanks for letting me know. Please keep taking your prenatal with the 4 mg folate every day, plus the iron. Keep the metformin for now and confirm with OB at your first visit, as they did last time. I've placed a referral back to your OB group; given the irregular cycles they will want a dating ultrasound. Call us or them if you have bleeding or significant pain.

documents.title: OB referral follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called OB office re referral. Received. They will contact pt directly for the new OB intake; pt reports first appointment they offered is mid-July due to provider leave, she accepted and is on their cancellation list. PCP informed.

conditions.label: Myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and hydrocephalus

reports.text: Transabdominal obstetric ultrasound. Single live intrauterine pregnancy, biometry consistent with 18 weeks. Fetal heart activity present. Amniotic fluid normal. Placenta anterior, clear of the cervix. Abdominal wall intact with normal cord insertion. Open posterior spinal defect in the lower spine with a protruding fluid-filled sac. Intracranial views show the posterior fossa changes of a Chiari II malformation with enlarged lateral ventricles. Limbs present; feet appear normally positioned.
reports.conclusion: Open spinal dysraphism with sac (myelomeningocele) with associated Chiari II malformation and ventriculomegaly.

documents.title: Obstetrics new prenatal visit letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group, letter to primary care.
Date of visit: 7/14/2025
Re: Shannon Wagner, 31 y/o G3P2002, 18w0d by today's ultrasound

She comes for her initial prenatal visit. She learned of the pregnancy about two months ago; irregular cycles from PCOS. Her last pregnancy, delivered here in 2022, was complicated by fetal gastroschisis. Continues prenatal vitamin with 4 mg folate, ferrous sulfate and metformin 500 mg twice daily.

Ultrasound today shows a lower spinal defect with a sac, along with the intracranial changes that accompany it: a Chiari II malformation and enlarged ventricles. This is a fetal myelomeningocele.

We spent a long time with her and her husband. Plan: detailed counseling with maternal-fetal medicine and pediatric neurosurgery, serial ultrasound for ventricular size and growth, and a planned cesarean delivery at a center with neonatal neurosurgery. Routine prenatal labs sent.
Allergies: latex, sulfa. Latex precautions are especially noted for delivery planning.

documents.title: PCP check-in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with Shannon after the OB letter came in about the baby's spine. She is shaken but organized; has appointments lined up with MFM and the neurosurgery team. Husband taking time off for the visits. Not sleeping well this week. Booked her in with me in a few weeks to check in properly.

Worry is constant in the background, sleep better than in July. Working reduced hours. No thoughts of self-harm. Taking prenatal, iron, metformin.

O: BP and HR normal. Weight appropriate for dates. Tearful briefly talking about the scans, otherwise composed. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.
GAD-7 9, PHQ-9 6.

A/P:
1. GAD in a high-stress pregnancy - supportive visit. She feels her support at home is good. Recheck after delivery or sooner by message.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - OB checking counts.
3. PCOS - metformin per OB.
Flu and updated COVID in October.

Outside obstetrics group, letter to primary care.
Date of visit: 9/17/2025
Re: Shannon Wagner, 27w2d, fetal myelomeningocele

Routine follow-up. For two weeks she has noticed being short of breath, more when lying flat and eased by sitting up. No chest pain, no cough, no wheezing. Maternal course otherwise smooth.

RR 18, HR 88, BP 120/75, SpO2 98% on room air. Lungs clear both sides. Heart sounds normal without murmur, rub or gallop. No leg swelling.
Hgb 11.5, Hct 34%, platelets 220K.

Assessment: physiologic dyspnea of pregnancy; normal oxygenation, clear exam and stable blood count. Reviewed reasons to call (chest pain, one-sided leg swelling, breathlessness at rest). Tdap given today.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.

events.reason: Facial hair, voice change, acne in pregnancy

reports.text: Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound with views of the adnexa. Both ovaries are enlarged with multiple thin-walled cysts: right ovary 3 cm, left ovary 4 cm. No solid component and no free fluid. Single live intrauterine pregnancy in cephalic position, amniotic fluid normal. No new fetal findings beyond the known spinal defect; fetal status reassuring.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral multicystic ovarian enlargement, right 3 cm, left 4 cm. Reassuring fetal status.

documents.title: Obstetrics prenatal visit letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group, letter to primary care.
Date of visit: 11/14/2025
Re: Shannon Wagner, 32 y/o, 35w4d, fetal myelomeningocele, PCOS

Seen with her husband, who is worried about changes in how she looks. Over about two months she has had much more facial hair, a lower voice and new acne. She denies headache, vision changes or abdominal pain.

BP 120/78, HR 72. Appears well. Facial hirsutism and temporal hair thinning noted.

Labs: Hgb 12.5, platelets 250K, fasting glucose 88. Total testosterone 150 ng/dL (non-pregnant female range 15-70). DHEA-S 180 ug/dL (non-pregnant female range 35-430).
Pelvic ultrasound: both ovaries enlarged with multiple cysts, 3 cm right and 4 cm left, no solid features. Baby without new findings.

Assessment: androgen excess in late pregnancy with bilateral multicystic ovarian enlargement and a normal DHEA-S, pointing to an ovarian rather than adrenal source. The appearance is benign and this pattern is expected to regress after delivery. Expectant management. We will repeat the pelvic ultrasound and testosterone at her postpartum visit. Planned cesarean at 37 weeks is unchanged.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.

documents.title: Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: OB said my testosterone is high and there are cysts on my ovaries and it should go away after the baby. Is this from my PCOS? I hate the hair and my voice sounds weird on the phone at work.

documents.title: RE: Question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Shannon, I saw the OB note. Pregnancy hormones can stimulate the ovaries this way late in pregnancy, and it usually settles over the weeks after delivery. They plan to recheck the ultrasound and the testosterone after the baby comes, which is the right next step. I know it is upsetting. Hang in there for the next couple of weeks, and let's get together after you are home.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, obstetrics service.
Admitted 11/24/2025, discharged 11/29/2025.
Patient: Shannon Wagner, 32 y/o G3P2002 at 37w0d.
Allergies: LATEX (type I), sulfa.

Reason for admission: scheduled cesarean for fetal myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and ventriculomegaly.

On arrival she reported feeling generally fine apart from malaise and occasional palpitations with more sweating, which she put down to late pregnancy. BP 118/76, HR 88. Clinically euthyroid: thyroid of normal size, nontender, no nodules; reflexes normal; no tremor.

Admission labs: AST 286, ALT 241, total bilirubin 2.6 (direct 1.9), glucose 61, PT 17.1 / INR 1.5, uric acid 8.9, creatinine 1.2, WBC 14.6, platelets 168K. Thyroid: TSH 0.31 (low), free T4 1.7 (at the upper limit), total T4 15.6 (high); hCG elevated for gestational age.

Assessment: acute fatty liver of pregnancy, diagnosed on admission labs. Thyroid pattern attributed to hCG stimulation and the pregnancy rise in binding protein; no treatment.

Course: dextrose infusion for glucose, plasma for the coagulopathy, and cesarean delivery the same morning in a latex-free room. Infant to the NICU with the neurosurgery team. Postoperative monitoring in the high-risk obstetric unit. Day 2: AST 198, ALT 176, bilirubin 3.0, INR 1.3. Glucose stable off dextrose by day 2. Day 5: AST 92, ALT 105, bilirubin 1.8, INR 1.1, glucose and creatinine normal. Incision clean.

Discharge medications: acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed, maximum 2 g per day while the liver recovers. Continue prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate, metformin 500 mg twice daily.
Follow-up: primary care within the week for liver tests and INR; obstetrics postpartum visit with repeat pelvic ultrasound and testosterone in about 6 weeks.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up, acute fatty liver of pregnancy

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up. Discharge summary reviewed: cesarean at 37 wks on 11/24, acute fatty liver of pregnancy picked up on admission labs, delivered the same day, liver numbers falling by discharge.

S: Home 4 days. Incision sore, using acetaminophen once or twice a day. Appetite back, no nausea, no yellowing, urine normal color. Palpitations and sweating gone. Baby still in the NICU; she and her husband are there most of the day. Tired. Mood ok under the circumstances.

O: Vitals reviewed, afebrile. Not jaundiced. Abdomen soft, incision clean and dry, no erythema. No edema.
PHQ-9 5, GAD-7 8.

A/P:
1. Acute fatty liver of pregnancy - improving. Hepatic panel and INR today. Acetaminophen ok at no more than 2 g a day for now.
2. Post-cesarean - healing well.
3. GAD/postpartum mood - screens mild, close follow-up given the NICU stay.
4. PCOS/iron - continue metformin, iron, prenatal.
Recheck in 4 weeks with labs, including thyroid tests since they were off in the hospital.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: AST 54 and ALT 61, down from the hundreds, bilirubin 1.1 and clotting time back to normal. Your liver is recovering the way we hoped. We'll repeat everything at the visit on the 29th.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
5 weeks post cesarean. She is sleeping in short stretches but feels physically much better. No abdominal pain, no jaundice, eating normally. Stopped the acetaminophen a week ago. Facial hair and acne starting to ease per her. OB postpartum visit 1/9.
Meds: metformin 500 bid, ferrous sulfate, prenatal.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Well appearing. Sclerae anicteric. Incision healed. Abdomen soft, nontender. Heart and lungs normal.
PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 7.

A/P
1. Acute fatty liver of pregnancy - clinically resolved, closing it on the problem list. Hepatic panel today to confirm.
2. Abnormal thyroid tests during pregnancy - TSH and free T4 today to make sure they have normalized.
3. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC and iron studies, continue iron.
4. PCOS - continue metformin. OB to recheck ovaries and testosterone 1/9.
5. GAD/postpartum mood - mild, stable. She will message if this slips.
Follow up in spring.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of your liver tests are normal now (AST 24, ALT 27, bilirubin 0.6), so the fatty liver of pregnancy has fully resolved. Thyroid tests are normal too (TSH 1.62, free T4 1.1), so those changes were from the pregnancy. Hemoglobin 11.8 and ferritin 16, a bit low after delivery; please keep up the iron daily. Happy new year.

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal pelvic ultrasound. Postpartum uterus, involuting, no retained products. Right and left ovaries normal in size; the previously seen cysts are no longer present. No adnexal mass, no free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal-sized ovaries with resolution of the previously seen bilateral ovarian cysts.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit letter
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside obstetrics group, letter to primary care.
Date of visit: 1/9/2026
Re: Shannon Wagner, postpartum after cesarean on 11/24/2025 complicated by acute fatty liver of pregnancy

Feels well. Incision healed. Facial hair and acne are fading. Your office's liver tests from 12/29 reviewed, normal.

Pelvic ultrasound today: ovaries normal in size, the bilateral cysts seen in November have resolved. Total testosterone 52 ng/dL, back in the normal range.

The androgen excess and ovarian enlargement of late pregnancy have resolved as expected. Continue metformin for PCOS, prenatal vitamin and iron. Routine gynecologic care going forward; Pap due 2026.
Allergies: latex, sulfa.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requesting renewal metformin 500 mg 1 tab BID #180. Last OV 12/29/25. Sent per PCP.

documents.title: Appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I was supposed to come back in the spring. Things are nuts with two little ones' appointments plus work. Can I push my checkup to later in the summer? I'll call when I know my schedule.

documents.title: RE: Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Of course. Call or message us whenever you're ready and we'll find a time that works. Your physical would be due any time after June.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily #90 and prenatal vitamin #90. Sent. Pt overdue for follow-up, reminder attached to the refill notification.
